hints.title: Clear positive denominators
hints.body: Every denominator is a positive exponential. Multiply each candidate by its denominator and collect powers with a common base.
hints.pitfall: The sign of an exponent is not the sign of the exponential.
hints.pause: Write comparable forms for the candidate inequalities.

hints.title: Compare exponent sums
hints.body: Use the given ordering to compare the exponents appearing in each candidate. A base above one preserves those exponent comparisons.
hints.recap: Compare exact powers through their exponents.
hints.pitfall: The gaps between x,y,z need not be equal.
hints.pause: Seek a candidate whose required bounds follow for every allowed triple.

recall.reminder: Compare exact powers through their exponents.

hints.title: Prove the complete bound
hints.body: If a candidate has two terms on one side, compare each individually with an appropriate term or common bound on the other side, then add the justified inequalities.
hints.recap: Compatible strict inequalities can be added.
hints.pitfall: Examples can refute alternatives but cannot prove a universal inequality.
hints.pause: Complete the universal proof and check counterexamples for any remaining alternatives.

recall.reminder: Compatible strict inequalities can be added.

solution:
Multiplying C by the positive quantity 5z5y gives 2·5x+y>5x+z+52z. Since y>z and x>z, both terms on the right are strictly less than 5x+y. Their sum is therefore strictly less than the left side, proving C for all permitted x,y,z.

For comparison, A and B fail at (x,y,z)=(4,3,2). D fails with y=3,z=2,x=3+log7(4/3): its right side is 4/3+1/7=31/21<2. Answer C.
knowledgePattern: Compare ordered exponents and construct counterexamples to rival bounds
